text: You just cracked open your sixth can of Coke today, and it's not even dinner.
Each can has about ten teaspoons of sugar.
That's more sugar than you should have in a whole day.
Your blood sugar shoots up, and your body pumps out insulin to bring it back down.
The acid hits your teeth, and every sip starts a new twenty minute acid attack.
Over time, the extra sugar gets stored as fat, and your risk of diabetes goes up.
In rare cases, people drinking liters a day lost so much potassium their muscles went weak.
Tag the friend who drinks Coke like water, and subscribe.
